review_method: Fresh visual inspection of the newly acquired official high-resolution New South Wales chapter, original embedded-map pixels, legends, text and Table 4.4 alongside the complete supplied selected baseline paths. Counts, bounds and adjacent-part endpoint continuity were recomputed from the selected geometries, with all parts and positions plotted unmodified. The earlier Figure 4.1 raster was also visually compared. Independent observations were recorded before source-worker comparison. This reviewer did not independently decode original packs or verify original HydroRIVERS source-coordinate equality. The review itself required no further external requests.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory target IDs. Reassessment of existing IDs does not increase the total.
included_evidence_limit: Public summaries include own factual observations, bibliography and bounded target metadata. Original map bytes, full selected paths and visual judgments are omitted and cannot be replayed by public validation. Both prior scope holds remain after reassessment; neither identity nor any scalar or reach-level product name is approved.

findings.follow_up_scope: Establish a direct Richmond River name or named-station identity tied to the complete selected New South Wales corridor before promoting representative identity. Resolve headwater or feeder, storage-interface, exact name-transition and coastal reach scope before any separately authorized product application. This bounded review does not prescribe geometry repair or authorize new acquisition.
findings.supported_name_scope: The complete selected New South Wales path runs southeast from a northwestern headwater, south through the upper and middle corridor, then southeast to a southern bend before turning east and northeast to the coast south of Lismore. Its regional geography remains compatible with the Richmond River candidate. In the newly acquired high-resolution chapter, neighbouring Clarence, Boyd, Macleay and Manning line names are legible, but no direct Richmond river-line label is established in the inspected Figures 4.1, 4.22–4.27, 4.34, 4.35 or 4.45. Figure 4.22 supplies a Richmond River catchment callout, and Table 4.4 a Richmond River entry in the River basin column for Lismore. Rocky Creek in Figure 4.35 labels an urban-storage symbol, not the complete selected river. The prior ambiguity about potentially blurred Richmond lettering is replaced for these checked views by a bounded no-direct-label finding. Representative identity and whole-group naming remain on hold after complete-path reassessment. Headwater or feeder names, exact river/storage relationships, name transitions and the coastal ending remain unassigned at reach level.
limits: The direct-name gap persists in the inspected high-resolution New South Wales maps despite clearly readable neighbouring river names. This is a bounded result for the cited figures, not a claim that no direct Richmond or Hastings evidence exists elsewhere.

Grey catchment callouts and entries in the River basin column do not establish which river name applies to the complete selected modeled path. A modeled MAIN_RIV/mainstem role does not establish one real-world name for every part.
Flow values, salinity and variability symbols, flood-class dots, storage triangles and wetland callouts do not supply named-station identities or exact selected river-reach names.
The high-resolution chapter and earlier low-resolution full report are editions of one publication and one source group. Their hydrographic dataset independence has not been verified.
Original HydroRIVERS source-coordinate equality, exact feeder and reach-name transitions, selected-path storage crossings, tidal boundaries and the surveyed mouth are not established.

The rendered sea ending differs from retained baseline source-endpoint metadata. Those metadata are not independently verified original HydroRIVERS coordinates; no river name is extended over that difference.

confidence.basis: The full selected New South Wales path remains geographically compatible with the Richmond River basin candidate. Higher-resolution maps clarify symbol roles and neighbouring names, but the cited views establish no direct selected-river name or named-station correspondence.
